why_this_file_exists: services.json (repo root) binds service_id -> destination account and is owned by D3. It does NOT carry the two other translations the gateway has to perform, because canonical_intent hashes STRINGS while the contract compares ADDRESSES: agent_id (a string the agent submits) -> the agent's G... account, and asset "CODE:ISSUER" -> the asset's SAC C... address (packages/canonical/SPEC.md 5). Both mappings must be public and deterministic or a reviewer cannot recompute intent_hash and line it up against the on-chain Decision.

agents.note: agent_id is the UTF-8 string hashed into canonical_intent field 2. address is what the contract stores in Decision.agent and require_auth()s. Nothing on-chain links the two; this row is the binding, exactly as SPEC.md 5 is the binding for asset.

assets.note: The Phase 1 settlement asset, pinned in packages/canonical/SPEC.md 5. Equal to Policy.allowed_asset for every registered agent, so intents in this asset can be Approved.

A second, deliberately NON-policy asset, issued by the AEGIS testnet merchant account. It exists for one reason: SOW 5.2 scenario 4 (AssetMismatch) has to produce evidence ON CHAIN. With only one asset in this table the gateway would reject a mismatching asset locally as 'unknown asset' and the contract would never rule on it, so the scenario would be demonstrated by gateway code rather than by the contract. With this row the intent resolves to a real SAC, reaches authorize(), and comes back as a stored Decision with reason_code AssetMismatch. No settlement path uses it and no agent policy allows it.

asset_derivation.rule: Each sac is a deterministic function of (network passphrase, asset code, issuer account) with no AEGIS-controlled input. Recompute either row rather than trusting it:

limitation: This file has the same standing as services.json: PUBLISHED, NOT ENFORCED. No contract storage commits to it. A gateway that hashed one agent_id string while passing a different agent Address would still produce a decision whose intent_hash verifies; the mismatch shows up only by reading this table. Phase 1 accepts that -- see DECISIONS.md #5 for the same trade-off on asset.
